Felipe! So, how was your weekend in Naples?
Honestly, it was the city that surprised me most this year.
I told you! What surprised you?
The street life. We stayed in a neighborhood where people sit outside until midnight.
And the traffic?
Crazy. But we had a taxi driver who told us the history of every street.
Did you find the pizzeria that I told you about?
Yes, the one which has no menu. Six tables, and the best pizza of my life.
That place is a hidden gem. Even the people from Milan do not know it.
And the funicular was a great tip. The view was breathtaking.
So the city is not what people say?
Not at all. The reputation is the smallest part of the story.
We stayed in a neighborhood where the locals eat out.
We met a taxi driver who told us everything.
It has a reputation which is not fair.
The best places are the ones that tourists never find.

Hi Felipe, it's Laura from the events team, with the details for the Milan trade fair. The hotel that we booked is ten minutes from the fair, so you can walk. The colleague who organizes our stand is Paolo, and he will meet you at the hotel on Monday morning. The fair finishes on Friday at noon. You told me you wanted to stay for the weekend, so I found a train which leaves Milan at two and arrives in Naples at a quarter to seven. If you prefer Florence, which is closer, let me know before Wednesday.

Felipe, it's Giulia. Laura told me you are going to Naples, and I am so happy, because it's the city where I grew up. Please don't listen to people who say it is dangerous. Three things. First, stay in the old center, which is where the life is. Second, there is a small pizzeria near my grandmother's street that has no menu. You sit down and they bring you the pizza that they made that day. Third, on Sunday, take the funicular, which is a little train that goes up the hill. The view of the bay from there is breathtaking. Send me a photo.
